title: Proper-open comparison for complexes from the etale site
statement:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be a
proper morphism between
Noetherian schemes, and $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$
open immersions with
$u j_1=j_2$. Fix a finite coefficient ring
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, and a
bounded-below etale complex
$L\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.
Writing $K=\nu_X^*L$ for pullback along
the comparison
morphism, there is a canonical isomorphism on the pro-etale site

$$
j_{2!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*j_{1!}K.
$$

Here $j_!$ is
extension by zero and
$Ru_*$ is the
derived direct image.
These maps are the identity for the identity proper map and commute
with composition of proper maps fixing $X$.

The schemes and morphism properties are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Here a Noetherian scheme means one admitting a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The coefficient notation is that of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]: $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. The coefficient ring is used through its constant sheaf of rings on each site; the objects of the derived categories are sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, not necessarily constant sheaves. Use [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] on the etale site, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] for the ordinary, uncompleted pro-etale derived direct image, [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] for $\nu$, and [def-weil-extension-by-zero] for the pro-etale $j_!$.

proof.text: Write $N_i=\nu_{T_i}^*$, $N_X=\nu_X^*$, $J_i=j^{\mathrm{et}}_{i!}$ and $P_i=j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{i!}$. The comparison inverse images are exact on finite-coefficient module sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]; the $J_i$ and $P_i$ are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Thus their termwise functors induce derived functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and preserve $D^+$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] to $j_i$ to obtain natural sheaf isomorphisms $\delta_i:N_iJ_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P_iN_X$. Apply each component in every degree of a complex. Naturality for each differential makes this a chain map, and its degreewise inverse is a chain map as well. These maps descend to a natural isomorphism on $D^+$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2). We keep the notation $\delta_i$ for that isomorphism. In particular $J_iL$ and $K=N_XL$ are bounded below. No constructibility assumption on $L$ is needed.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha^e_u:J_2L\to R u_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L$ be the specified etale map of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Its hypotheses hold: the same proper $u$, opens $j_i$, equation $u j_1=j_2$, finite commutative coefficient ring, and bounded-below $L$ are given. It is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso]. Properness includes finite type and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]; finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separatedness implies quasi-separatedness [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Therefore [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], applied to the bounded-below etale complex $J_1L$ from step 1, gives a natural isomorphism
$$D_{u,M}:N_2R u_{\mathrm{et},*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}R u_{\mathrm{proet},*}N_1M,\qquad M\in D^+(T_{1,\mathrm{et}},\Lambda),$$
compatible with identities and composites. Specify $D_{u,M}$ to be the named counit-mate $b_{u,M}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]: it is the adjoint transpose of $N_1(\varepsilon^e_{u,M})\circ a_{u,Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}M}^{-1}$, where $a_u$ is the specified pullback comparison. That node proves invertibility of this very map, so no arbitrary isomorphism between the two objects is chosen. Neither $R u_*$ is being asserted exact on sheaves.

proof.text:
Define the pro-etale map to be the following composite in $D^+(T_{2,\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{u,L}:P_2K&\xrightarrow{\delta_{2,L}^{-1}}N_2J_2L
\xrightarrow{N_2(\alpha^e_{u,L})}N_2R u_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L\\
&\xrightarrow{D_{u,J_1L}}R u_{\mathrm{proet},*}N_1J_1L
\xrightarrow{R u_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\delta_{1,L})}R u_{\mathrm{proet},*}P_1K.
\end{aligned}$$
Every arrow is an isomorphism by steps 1 and 2 and functoriality, so their composite is an isomorphism. This specifies the claimed canonical map, without choosing a representative or an inverse of an unspecified existence witness. Its naturality in $L$ follows by composing the natural maps used in steps 1 and 2.

proof.text:
Check coherence explicitly. Let $v:T_2\to T_3$ be another proper map fixing the open $X$, with $j_3=vj_2$, and write $N_3,J_3,P_3,\delta_3$ similarly. The composite $vu$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], and $(vu)j_1=j_3$ by associativity and the two given equations, so step 3 defines $\beta_{vu,L}$. The complex $Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L$ lies in $D^+$: it is isomorphic by $\alpha^e_u$ to $J_2L$, which is bounded below by step 1. Thus both arguments of the naturality square below lie in the domain of $D_v$. Suppress $L$ and canonical direct-image composition isomorphisms in this calculation. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition], $\alpha^e_{vu}=(R v_{\mathrm{et},*}\alpha^e_u)\alpha^e_v$. By the composite compatibility in [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image],
$$D_{vu,J_1L}=(R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}D_{u,J_1L})\,D_{v,R u_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L}.$$
Naturality of $D_v$ for the morphism $\alpha^e_u:J_2L\to R u_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L$ reads
$$D_{v,Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}J_1L}\,N_3(R v_{\mathrm{et},*}\alpha^e_u)
=R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}(N_2\alpha^e_u)\,D_{v,J_2L}.$$
Substituting these two equalities into the formula of step 3 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{vu,L}
={}&R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}\bigl(R u_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\delta_{1,L})\,D_{u,J_1L}\,N_2(\alpha^e_{u,L})\bigr)\,
D_{v,J_2L}\,N_3(\alpha^e_{v,L})\,\delta_{3,L}^{-1}\\
={}&R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\beta_{u,L})\,\beta_{v,L}.
\end{aligned}$$
In the last equality insert $R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\delta_{2,L}^{-1})R v_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\delta_{2,L})=1$ and use the two definitions from step 3. For $u=\mathrm{id}$ the cited etale map and $D_{\mathrm{id}}$ are identities, and the remaining factors are $\delta_i\delta_i^{-1}=1$. This proves exactly the asserted identity and composition laws.
